Today Apple is celebrating the opening of its advanced manufacturing center in Houston, Texas. Here are the relevant details.

Apple will train business leaders at its brand new advanced manufacturing center in Houston

Today Apple opened its brand new Advanced Manufacturing Center (AMC) in Houston. The center provides small and medium-sized businesses with free training and educational programs, giving them hands-on access to the most advanced equipment, interactive labs, and various tools to accelerate innovation. The Advanced Manufacturing Center is located in the same Houston facility that is responsible for producing and shipping Apple’s advanced AI servers, and will begin producing Mac mini within this year. […] Apple CEO Tim Cook said: “In just nine months, we have invested hundreds of millions of dollars into this Houston facility. We have built the factory, started production, and have already shipped the first batch of advanced AI servers out of the plant. Today, we are delighted to open this brand new Advanced Manufacturing Center, a place where business leaders, workers, and students can learn the same innovative processes we use to manufacture Apple’s most groundbreaking products. We are also looking forward to starting production of Mac mini later this year. We believe in the strength of American workers and American creativity, and we are moving forward at an astonishing pace, because what we want to create is not just great products—what we want to build is the future of American manufacturing.”

Tim Cook announced his trip to Houston via social media, making a special trip to attend the opening event. Guests attending the launch ceremony included U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, U.S. Senator Ted Cruz, Houston Mayor John Whitmire, U.S. Representative Christian Menefee, and Harris County Precinct One Commissioner Rodney Ellis.

The Advanced Manufacturing Center spans 20,000 square feet, where Apple’s experts will “directly share their knowledge with participating businesses and entrepreneurs, helping to accelerate the development of smart manufacturing in the United States.”

The first batch of business leaders arrived today to take part in the inaugural training session. The day’s topics focused on smart manufacturing technologies, including “machine learning–driven quality control and advanced automation.”
